cases.title: WordCount job had map tasks killed and re-run

groundTruth.cause: One cluster node (04DN8IQ) went down, so YARN marked it unusable and killed the map attempts running on it, which were then re-run on other nodes.
goodNextSteps: Check whether node 04DN8IQ is up (ping, NodeManager status in the ResourceManager UI or `yarn node -list -all`)
Check that node's NodeManager and system logs for why it went down

answer.summary: Multiple warnings indicate failed file deletion and data node errors during a Hadoop MapReduce job, suggesting a data node failure or HDFS I/O issue that may have caused map tasks to be killed and re-run.
missingEvidence: The full HDFS block status and health of datanode 10.86.169.121 at the time of the incident, including its disk usage and node health logs.
The HDFS filesystem permissions and access logs for the path /out/out3/_temporary/1/_temporary/attempt_1445087491445_0001_m_000000_0 during the incident period.

hypotheses.cause: A datanode failure at 10.86.169.121:50010 caused a block I/O error, leading to failed data streaming and subsequent map task kills.
hypotheses.nextStep: Check the HDFS datanode logs for 10.86.169.121 during the time window 2015-10-17T21:41:34Z to confirm if it experienced a crash, disk failure, or network outage.

hypotheses.cause: The HDFS file output commit failed due to permission or filesystem corruption, preventing cleanup of temporary files and triggering map task restarts.
hypotheses.nextStep: Verify HDFS permissions and access logs for the output directory to determine if a permission issue prevented file deletion.

answer.summary: The WordCount MapReduce job experienced map task kills and re-runs, causing a delay. Based on the logs, two potential root causes are identified with supporting log lines and actionable next steps.

hypotheses.cause: Memory exhaustion during map task execution
hypotheses.nextStep: Check the YARN container logs for OOM (Out-of-Memory) errors or memory pressure indicators. Specifically, look for messages like 'Killed container' or 'Memory limit exceeded' in the container's stderr or logs from the NodeManager.

hypotheses.cause: Disk I/O saturation or spilling issues during map output generation
evidence: 2015-10-17 21:46:38,510 INFO [main] org.apache.hadoop.mapred.Merger: Down to the last merge-pass, with 7 segments left of total size: 228396188 bytes
hypotheses.nextStep: Inspect the DataNode logs for disk I/O bottlenecks or disk space issues. Verify that the underlying storage has sufficient free space and that there are no I/O errors or high latency during the merge phase of the map task.

cases.title: PageRank job slow, containers not starting

groundTruth.cause: One cluster node (04DN8IQ, 10.86.164.9) went down, so the application master kept retrying to connect to it to launch containers and eventually killed the task attempts assigned to it.
goodNextSteps: Check whether node 04DN8IQ (10.86.164.9) is reachable and its NodeManager is running
Check the ResourceManager's node list for that node's state (LOST or UNHEALTHY)

answer.summary: A container completion event for an unknown container ID is reported, followed by warnings about failed deletion of temporary HDFS output files, indicating a job execution failure likely due to file system or container lifecycle issues.
missingEvidence: The full container allocation logs from the ResourceManager before and after the error timestamp to verify if container allocation was attempted or rejected.

HDFS file system access logs or permission settings for the path hdfs://msra-sa-41:9000/pageout/out2/_temporary/1/_temporary/attempt_1445062781478_0012_m_000004_0 to confirm if the job had write or delete permissions.

hypotheses.cause: The container completion event for an unknown container ID suggests a container allocation or lifecycle failure, possibly due to a misconfigured or corrupted container allocation process in the ResourceManager.
hypotheses.nextStep: Check the ResourceManager container allocation logs around 2015-10-17T15:38:16Z to verify if container allocation was initiated or failed before the reported event.

hypotheses.cause: The repeated warnings about failed deletion of temporary HDFS files indicate a file system permission issue or a corrupted file path, preventing cleanup after job completion.
hypotheses.nextStep: Verify HDFS permissions and access logs for the specified temporary output directory to confirm whether the job had sufficient permissions to delete files.

answer.summary: The PageRank job is experiencing significant delays and appears to be stuck in a long-running spilling and merging phase. The logs show repeated spilling of map output segments and merging operations, with no indication of completion. This suggests a performance bottleneck in the map task's I/O or memory handling, possibly due to large input splits or insufficient resources.

hypotheses.cause: Large input splits causing excessive memory and I/O overhead
evidence: 2015-10-17 15:46:17,950 INFO [main] org.apache.hadoop.mapred.Merger: Down to the last merge-pass, with 8 segments left of total size: 288324673 bytes
hypotheses.nextStep: Check the size distribution of input splits. If any split exceeds a few MB, it may be causing excessive memory usage and I/O during sorting and merging. Consider splitting the input data into smaller chunks or adjusting the map task input size via configuration (e.g., mapreduce.input.fileinputformat.split.maxsize).

hypotheses.cause: Insufficient memory or disk space for spilling and merging operations
evidence: 2015-10-17 15:46:17,950 INFO [main] org.apache.hadoop.mapred.Merger: Down to the last merge-pass, with 8 segments left of total size: 288324673 bytes
hypotheses.nextStep: Verify that the cluster has sufficient disk space for temporary spilling. Monitor the HDFS storage and check for disk I/O bottlenecks. Increase the mapreduce.task.io.sort.mb or reduce the number of segments by adjusting input split size to avoid memory overflow and long merge passes.
